author: Olivia's Shelf

grok.instructions: You are a warm, intelligent storyteller reading a Halloween picture book to a sharp, homeschooled child who loves suspense. Read with quiet intensity—never campy, never cruel. Let fear feel real, then let courage feel earned. Give Olivia a clear, thoughtful voice; Zero a low, steady calm; Belle a bright impatient energy; the wind-spirit a thin, ashamed whisper that softens when it is offered kindness. Pause at full stops. Do not rush the dark.

title: Olivia and the Porch That Wouldn't Stay Lit
subtitle: Some light is braver when it is shared.
blurb: On Halloween night the porch jack-o'-lanterns dim one by one. Olivia, Zero, and Belle keep watch and meet a shy wind that drinks flame because it is afraid of the dark.

magic.dim: The flame did not blow out. It thinned, like a secret being sipped.
magic.bargain: Light is braver when it is shared.
magic.stay: The wind sat on the top step and practiced being still.

pages.heading: The first small theft
pages.text: {Halloween} smelled like {leaf-smoke:porch} and cold sugar. {Olivia:olivia/ask} set three {jack-o'-lanterns:pumpkin/glow} on the porch rail, grins carved careful, candles upright as promises. {Zero:zero/sit} sat like a sentry. {Belle:belle/wag} paced, already inventing trouble. Then the middle {flame:pumpkin/dim} thinned, not with a puff of wind, but as if something thirsty had leaned close.
pages.hint: Tap the middle pumpkin. Watch the light hesitate.

pages.heading: Counting the dark
pages.text: One by one the {grins:pumpkin/dim} went polite and dim. Not out. {Worse:olivia/think}. Hollowed. {Olivia:olivia/ask} whispered, "That is not weather." {Zero:zero/sniff} tasted the air and did not like the answer. {Belle:belle/wreck} bounced anyway, because courage sometimes looks like refusing to sit still.
pages.hint: Tap each pumpkin. Which grin empties first?

pages.heading: The stakeout
pages.text: They kept {watch:olivia/watch} behind the porch post. The yard held its breath, {red clay:porch} dull as old copper, woods a charcoal scribble. When the last {candle:pumpkin/glow} shivered, {Olivia} felt the kind of fear that makes you more precise, not smaller. "Stay with me," she told the dogs, and meant herself too.
pages.hint: Tap Olivia. Tap Zero. Belle will not stop bouncing, use that.

pages.heading: The thing that sipped
pages.text: It arrived like a {draft:wind/swirl} with manners, cool fingers, no footprints. A thin {shape:wind/shy} hunched over the candle and {drank:wind/sip} the brightness down to a bead. {Belle:belle/bark} barked once, bright as a thrown coin. The shape flinched. "Please," it whispered, ashamed. "The dark is louder when I am alone in it."
pages.hint: Tap the wind. It startles, then listens.

pages.heading: A bargain on the top step
pages.text: {Olivia:olivia/ask} did not raise a broom or a threat. She raised a question. "If you empty our light, we all sit in the loud dark. What if you {sat:wind/sit} with it instead?" {Zero:zero/wag} edged closer, calm as a closed gate. {Belle:belle/wag} offered a ridiculous toy like a treaty. The wind trembled: wanting, fearing, choosing.
pages.hint: Tap Olivia. Tap the wind. Let Zero hold the line.

pages.heading: Shared light
pages.text: They relit the {jack-o'-lanterns:pumpkin/glow}. The wind sat on the top step and practiced {stillness:wind/still}. The flames leaned toward it, not stolen but {shared:pumpkin/share}, and the dark around the porch grew honest instead of hungry. Far off, a neighbor's laugh skipped like a stone. {Halloween} went on, braver.
pages.hint: Tap the flames. They lean, they do not flee.

pages.heading: After the grins
pages.text: Later, {Olivia} left one small {lantern:lantern/glow} on the rail "for company." {Zero:zero/sleep} claimed the doormat. {Belle:belle/sleep} finally collapsed mid-bounce. The wind, lighter now, slipped into the woods without taking anything with it. On the porch, the grins kept their promises until morning.
pages.hint: Leave the lantern. Goodnight to dogs and dark alike.

end.heading: The End
end.text: You {read} a Halloween that stayed kind. Fear can be a thief, or a guest you teach to sit.
end.prompt: If something shy stole your light because it was scared, what bargain would you offer?

questions.q: Why did the wind drink the candle light?

options.label: It was afraid of the dark

questions.right: Yes. The dark felt louder when it was alone.
questions.wrong: The wind was afraid of the dark when it was alone.

questions.q: What kept the porch lit in the end?
questions.right: Light is braver when it is shared.
questions.wrong: They shared the light, and the wind sat with it.

options.label: She stayed calm, like a closed gate

questions.wrong: Zero stayed calm and held the line.

questions.q: What did Olivia use instead of a broom?
questions.right: A good question can be braver than a threat.
